text:
maya (support): FYI — customer AcmeCorp reporting increased 429s and large latency spikes on Dedicated NA-Central around 10:01 UTC. They say autoscale didn't kick and fallback to eu-west increased p95.
liam (sre): Noted. Any error samples? request IDs?
maya (support): Sent logs in the ticket: repeated placement failures, errors: "insufficient_gpus" then "placement_timeout". Also a couple auth failures: "token_validation_failed" after failover.
andre (infra): Pulling infra metrics now. I can already see GPU utilization on na-central pool spiking to 97% on some nodes, while others show noisy neighbor pattern (one pod hogging 3x expected memory).
zhen (oncall): Can we confirm autoscaler logs? Maybe scale policy hit limit. Running: `kubectl logs -n infra autoscaler-ctrl`
ops-bot: autoscaler-ctrl pod restarted at 10:02:13 UTC due to OOM; last 3 restarts in 10m.
liam (sre): OOM on autoscaler explains no scale out. Why did autoscaler OOM? Check heap/gc, recent rollout?
andre (infra): There was a config change 09:58 — tightened scaling cooldown from 90s to 30s in the policy. Might increase churn. Also rolling deploy of autoscaler image 09:50. Image didn't change major version but new startup flags present.
maya (support): Customer repro steps in ticket: run 500 concurrent streams w/ seq_len 512 prompt, tokens ~1k, run for 5 minutes. They saw errors at ~2:30 in.
liam (sre): Repro matches our surge profile. Two things we should do now: 1) mitigate for customer—manually provision burst-capacity + route their traffic to dedicated backfill pool; 2) remediate autoscaler OOM.
zhen (oncall): I'm manually adding 4 gpus to na-central-burst for now. Running `redwoodctl capacity add --pool na-central-burst --gpus 4`
ops-bot: capacity change request accepted, provisioning started (ETA 4m).
andre (infra): Also starting controlled eviction on noisy tenant seen on node gpu-7 . Command: `infractl evict-workload --node gpu-7 --label tenant=unknown-noise`
liam (sre): Eviction ok but watch for transient token errors — we saw token_validation_failed after failover because some auth sessions were sticky to region. Need to flush session caches in auth proxy for affected tenants.
maya (support): I've asked customer to retry with new endpoint and to share a fresh request id if they still hit 429s.
zhen (oncall): Autoscaler logs show OOM at 10:02 due to unbounded goroutine growth in watcher loop after config parsing started failing for one policy. Rolling back autoscaler to previous stable image v2.3.1 now.
andre (infra): Rolling back, redeploying with increased memory 1.5Gi -> 3Gi.
ops-bot: autoscaler v2.3.1 deployed successfully at 10:08:22 UTC.
liam (sre): After redeploy, scale events observed at 10:09 and new nodes joined. P95 for affected customer started dropping from 1.2s to 220ms after failover draining finished.
maya (support): Customer confirms initial positive signal — fewer 429s. Still seeing some requests hit eu-west with increased latency (expected) but functional.
andre (infra): Follow-ups: revert cooldown to prior value, add memory limit, add healthcheck on config parsing. Also add a preflight test to PRs that change scaling flags.
zhen (oncall): Incident action items: 1) patch autoscaler to avoid goroutine leak; 2) add alert for autoscaler OOMs; 3) implement tenant isolation quota to reduce noisy neighbor risk; 4) run capacity soak tests for 2 weeks in na-central.
liam (sre): Assigning owners: andre for autoscaler patch, zhen for alerts and quotas, maya to coordinate customer comms and postmortem.
maya (support): Noted. I'll send a short update to AcmeCorp and schedule a postmortem doc. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
liam (sre): Marking incident resolved for active mitigation — monitoring for 24h. If p95 climbs again we'll escalate to SRE oncall paging.
ops-bot: Incident status changed to "mitigated" at 10:15 UTC.
